investigation.title: Remote Agents: Swarm Gateway 502 — All Three Remote-Agent Checks Failing with Shared Bad-Gateway Error
investigation.summary: All three remote-agent checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed at 2026-08-27T17:01–17:02Z with an identical 502 bad-gateway error indicating the swarm provisioning gateway (an AWS ELB in us-east-2) was unreachable. Because the failure is upstream of agent creation, no evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was collected, and all contract assertions are unverifiable.
investigation.rootCause: The swarm gateway — the AWS ELB endpoint targeted by POST /api/agents → http://[REDACTED].elb.us-east-2.amazonaws.com/v1/agents — was unreachable at the time of the eval run. The production-api layer returned HTTP 502 with code "bad_gateway" and the message "swarm gateway unreachable during agent provisioning: error sending request for url (http://[REDACTED].elb.us-east-2.amazonaws.com/v1/agents)". This is a shared upstream infrastructure dependency failure: all three sibling checks hit the same endpoint and received the same error within a 34-second window, producing zero evidence output. The root cause is localized to the swarm gateway / ELB layer in us-east-2, not to the eval runner code or the production-api application logic itself. No user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence, so impact is scoped to this observability eval run.

investigation.title: image-generation-stream Eval Failure: OpenAI API Credit Balance Exhausted on /api/generate/image/stream
investigation.summary: The image-generation-stream eval failed because the OpenAI API key used by the eval runner has no remaining credits, causing the upstream image generation call to return a hard error (code: credit_balance_exhausted). The stream terminated with a generation_error frame instead of the required generation_completed frame, so both contract assertions — frameTypes contains "generation_completed" and imageUrlPresent equals true — were violated. This is an eval infrastructure / API credential failure, not a confirmed user-facing product outage.
investigation.rootCause: The OpenAI account associated with the API key used by the eval runner at /api/generate/image/stream has exhausted its credit balance. The upstream API rejected the image generation request with error type "insufficient_quota" and code "credit_balance_exhausted", causing the server to emit a generation_error SSE frame and terminate the stream without ever emitting a generation_completed frame or an artifact URL. Both required contract assertions therefore fail. The failure is localized to the eval runner's OpenAI credential/billing configuration, not to the stream routing or frame-emission logic itself.
proof: failed-check.message: OpenAI error body contains type=insufficient_quota and code=credit_balance_exhausted, confirming the upstream API rejected the request due to zero remaining credits.

failed-check.evidence: frameTypes observed = [generation_start, generation_start, generation_progress, generation_error, message]; generation_completed is absent, and imageUrlPresent=false, directly matching both violated assertions.
failed-check.evidence: The generation_error frame data.message field reproduces the full OpenAI error JSON verbatim, confirming the error originated at the OpenAI API boundary.

failed-check.timing: latencyMs=2243, far below the warningLatencyMs=180000 threshold, indicating the request was rejected immediately by OpenAI rather than timing out or hanging — consistent with a quota rejection rather than a network or routing fault.

possibleCauses: Primary — OpenAI credit balance exhausted on the account/key used by the eval runner: The error code credit_balance_exhausted is explicit and unambiguous (failed-check.message, failed-check.evidence).
Secondary — Wrong or expired OpenAI API key configured for the eval environment: A key belonging to a depleted or deactivated account would produce the same error response.
Tertiary — Eval runner is using a free-tier or trial OpenAI account whose quota has been consumed: Free-tier accounts have hard credit caps that produce this exact error type.

Lower probability — The AURA_STATUS_IMAGE_MODEL environment variable resolves to a model (default: gpt-image-2) that is only available on paid plans, and the configured key does not have access to that model tier; however, the error code is specifically credit_balance_exhausted rather than a model-access error, making this less likely.
